svg.title: Bandwidth, not kernel shape, decides what a density estimate says
svg.desc: Three kernel density estimates of the same fifty observations, drawn from a bimodal population, at three bandwidths. At a bandwidth of 0.09 the estimate is a spiky rendering of the sample with many spurious modes, because variance dominates. At 0.42 the two true modes appear cleanly. At 1.30 the estimate is a single broad bump and the bimodality is gone, because bias dominates. A rug of tick marks beneath each panel shows the same observations in all three.

g.text: The same fifty observations, three bandwidths, three conclusions
bias grows as h² and variance falls as 1/(nh), so h* ∝ n^(−1/5)
Kernel shape costs a few percent; bandwidth changes the answer. Spend the effort on h.
